headline: Follow the uphill half with binary search
statement: Return an index of any peak in nums, where a peak is strictly greater than its neighbors. Adjacent values differ, and values outside the array are treated as negative infinity. The algorithm must take O(log n) time.
intuition: Compare the middle value with its right neighbor. If the slope rises, a peak must exist to the right: either the rise eventually ends or the final element is a peak. A falling slope similarly guarantees a peak on the left including the middle.
approach: If nums[mid] < nums[mid+1], move left to mid+1. Otherwise move right to mid.
correctness: The current interval always contains a peak compatible with its bounding slopes. On a rising middle edge, the right side contains a peak; on a falling edge, the left side through mid contains one. The chosen interval shrinks without losing all peaks. A singleton satisfying these boundaries is a valid peak.
bruteForce: Scan every index and compare its neighbors, taking O(n) time.

complexity.explanation: The interval approximately halves each iteration and uses three indices.

pitfalls: A peak need not be the global maximum.
A monotone array has a peak at one endpoint.
